title: The five-level model (book)
caption: The book's layered map: wire/link, transport, topology, fabric behavior, cluster design. The packet follows the same order; each level is where a different assumption from generic networking breaks.

title: PAM4 vs NRZ (book)
caption: Four levels carry 2 bits per symbol where NRZ carried 1, at the price of a third of the SNR margin, which is why FEC is now mandatory and costs hundreds of nanoseconds.

title: Physical reach ladder (book)
caption: Package at millimeters, DAC at 1-3 m, AOC at 3-30 m, optics past 30 m. The packet uses the ladder to explain why spine links are pairs of ~20 W pluggable modules.

title: GPUDirect data path (book)
caption: The NIC reading and writing GPU HBM directly, no CPU staging. The packet's Level 2 keeps this as the reason RDMA collectives can reach line rate at all.

title: Rail-optimized topology (book)
caption: The book's rail diagram: same-index GPUs share a switch path, collapsing 3 hops to 1 for traffic the layout localizes. Our cut figure draws the cost side (oversubscription) of the same design space.

title: Incast flow (book)
caption: The book's many-to-one incast illustration with 256 senders. Ours recomposes the same event as a buffer-survival timeline: 640 us of hold against a <5 us overflow.
